title: String Enums
definition: Enums where each member must be explicitly initialized with a string literal, providing better readability at runtime than numeric enums.
simpleExplanation: If a numeric enum is a secret code (Admin = 1), a String Enum is a name tag (Admin = 'ADMIN'). When you look at the raw data in your database or logs, you don't see a random '1', you actually see the word 'ADMIN', which makes debugging much easier.
realWorldExample: Defining strict API routes: `enum Routes { Login = '/auth/login', Dashboard = '/app/dashboard' }`.
useCases: Database storage where exact strings are preferred over IDs

basic: Do string enums auto-increment like numeric enums?
intermediate: Why are string enums easier to debug than numeric enums?
advanced: Do string enums support reverse mapping?

answers.question: Do they auto-increment?
answers.answer: No. Because they are strings, TypeScript cannot automatically 'add 1' to the previous value. You must explicitly set the string value for every single member.

answers.question: Do they support reverse mapping?
answers.answer: No. Only numeric enums support reverse mapping (`Enum[1]`). String enums only go one way.
